title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage with designed, built and proved
when: Runs `lathe check` on the broken-tests fixture.
then: Expects the Errors section, then Warnings, then Coverage, with `[test-file-missing-id] EX-LEND-INV01-T:` among the errors and `[technical-file-missing] EX-LEND-DS01-SV:` among the warnings.

title: The check exits 1 on any error and 0 otherwise, whatever the warnings
when: Runs `lathe check` on the broken-tests fixture and on the clean fixture.
then: Expects status 1 for the broken fixture, and status 0 with `0 errors, 0 warnings.` for the clean one.

title: With --json the check prints each product's whole workspace
when: Runs `lathe check --json`.
then: Expects its output to parse to one product, the root `.`, with the same `Workspace` that `loadWorkspace` returns.

title: Data the store refuses loads no records, and each refusal is a data-refused error
when: Loads a product whose command names an aggregate that does not exist.
then: Expects no records loaded and every problem a data-refused error, naming the missing aggregate.

title: A link from a record of one product to a record of another is refused, whatever the relation; an ID in text is not a link
when: Adds a second product `NX` with a view `NX-V01`, and points the data file's `presents` link at `NX-V01`.
then: Expects one `data-refused` error whose message says `EX-LEND-UC02-FL01-S01 is in product EX`.

title: Data the store refuses is an error naming the file and line, not a crash
when: Runs lathe check on a product whose data/product.jsonl gives a column the table lacks.
then: Expects exit status 1 and a data-refused error naming data/product.jsonl:1.

title: Every problem names its check and, when it has one, its record
when: Loads the complete product with every `presents` link removed, its specification tests not automated yet, one test's file silent and one source file missing, so that more than three checks report problems.
then: Expects every problem in every fixture to name its check in lower case with hyphens, to end as a sentence, and to name its record, whose ID its message contains.

title: A test at a level its kind does not allow is a warning
when: Loads the complete product with its constraint tests and flow test `EX-LEND-UC01-FL01-T` at `service`, then with its constraint tests at `integration`. Loads the complete product with its pattern rule test at each level.
then: Expects one `test-level-not-allowed` warning each, the flow test's saying to run it at system, browser and the constraint test's at unit, integration; and none at `integration`. Expects no test-level-not-allowed warning at any of them.

title: A test run at a level its kind does not allow is a warning; one its kind allows is not
when: With a complete product, runs a constraint test at browser, then at integration.
then: A warning listing the allowed levels; none at integration.

title: A new check needs only a new check row
when: Adds a check row `every-loan-command` to the complete product, reporting each command of the Loan aggregate, with no change to the engine.
then: Expects exactly two `every-loan-command` warnings, for `EX-LEND-CMD01` and `EX-LEND-CMD03`, each saying 'Command <id> changes a loan.'.

title: Checks can read every typed table, with file facts already computed
when: Runs a check that counts the record registry, the links, the test table and the meta-model tables, and reads the file facts.
then: Expects the counts to match the workspace, and each file fact (the file exists, the test's file names its ID) to match the fixture.

title: A check reads the maxChildren setting from the product_setting table
when: Loads a product whose own check reads its `product_setting` row.
then: Expects the check to see `max_children` 3.

title: The record_group view covers a product kind's group_name and a flow step's path
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and adds records of it, grouped and ungrouped.
then: Expects record_group to give the grouped record its group as written, leave out the ungrouped one, and give a flow step its path.

title: Every check runs, in position order, even after one fails
when: Runs three check rows, the second of which reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects their problems in position order, with the failing check reported as one error saying it could not run.

title: A product check runs after Lathe's checks, against the same tables
when: Loads the complete product with its own check `every-event-heard`, which reads the domain_event and hears tables.
then: Expects one `every-event-heard` warning for `EX-LEND-EV02`: 'Domain event EX-LEND-EV02 is heard by no policy.'.

title: A product check reports only on its own product's records, and on none
when: Loads two products, where one has a check that returns every domain and one row with no record.
then: Expects its problems for its own product's domain and for no record, and none for the other product's domain.

title: Without check rows of its own only Lathe's checks run
when: Loads the complete product with its own checks and `src/dates.ts` missing, and sets aside its own checks' problems.
then: Expects every other problem to come from one of Lathe's checks: `technical-file-missing` and `not-built`.

title: A product check's name comes from its row, not from a check column its query returns
when: Loads the product check `every-event-heard`, whose query returns `house-rule` in a check column.
then: Expects no problem under `house-rule`.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused by the store, so it never runs
when: Writes a product check named `view-unused`, like one of Lathe's, into the product's `data/check.jsonl` and loads it.
then: Expects one `data-refused` error saying `check view-unused is already on lathe/data/check.jsonl`.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
when: Loads a product whose check `broken` reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects one error with no record under `broken`, saying the check could not run.

title: A product names no checks folder: lathe.config.json refuses a checks setting, since checks are rows
when: Loads a product whose `lathe.config.json` names a `checks` folder.
then: Expects the load to stop with `unknown setting "checks"`.

title: A record with more children of one kind than maxChildren is a warning naming the parent, kind and count
when: With `max_children` 3, gives use case `EX-LEND-UC01` four UC requirements.
then: Expects one `too-many-children` warning on `EX-LEND-UC01` saying 'Use case EX-LEND-UC01 has 4 children of kind uc_requirement, more than the 3'.

title: A record's tests are never counted, however many it holds
when: Adds 20 use case tests under one UC requirement of the complete product.
then: Expects no `too-many-children` warning under the default limit.

title: Too many children and a lone child are warnings, never errors
when: Loads the fixtures that break `too-many-children` and `lone-child` and reads the severity of every problem they report.
then: Expects every `too-many-children` and `lone-child` problem to be a warning, and no errors in either fixture.

title: Without the setting, maxChildren is 15
when: With no `product_setting` row, gives use case `EX-LEND-UC01` sixteen UC requirements.
then: Expects one `too-many-children` warning saying it has 16 children of kind uc_requirement, more than the 15.

title: maxChildren is read from the product's product_setting row, max_children
when: Loads a product whose `product_setting` row gives `max_children` 3.
then: Expects `too-many-children` on the three records over 3, each message naming the product's max_children setting.

title: An aggregate or read model with one use case is not a lone child, nor is a flow's path with one step
when: Loads the complete product, whose use cases each sit alone with their aggregate, then adds a query use case and a flow path of one step.
then: Expects no `lone-child` warning in either.

title: A group's members are counted among their parent's children of one kind; a group of two, and children with no group, are not reported
when: Loads a use case with requirements in a group of two and one with no group, then with a group of two and a group of one.
then: Expects no `lone-child` warning for the first, and one for the second naming the group of one and its member.

title: A flow's steps are counted per path
when: Loads a flow with three steps on its main path and three on refused under a limit of 3, then four on refused.
then: Expects no warning, then one naming the refused path.

title: too-many-children counts grouped requirements per group, groups compared in any case
when: With `max_children` 2, gives a use case three requirements in the group Limits (one written `limits ` in lower case with a trailing space) and one in Other, beside its ungrouped one.
then: Expects one `too-many-children` warning, saying it has 3 children of kind uc_requirement in group Limits.

title: too-many-children counts a product kind's records per group_name
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and puts seven of its records under one domain, in two groups of two and one of three, under a limit of 2; then only the two groups of two.
then: Expects one warning, naming the group of three; with only the groups of two, four records under the domain, none.

title: too-many-children counts a domain's use cases per aggregate or read model they sit with
when: With max_children 2, gives the complete product's Loan aggregate two use cases besides one of the Tool and one of the Free tools read model; then a third of the Loan.
then: Expects no warning, then one too-many-children warning on the domain naming the Loan aggregate and saying to split the aggregate or read model they sit with.

title: A group with one member is a lone-child warning on its parent, standard rules included
when: Puts every standard rule of the complete product in the group `Imports`, and its API requirements, with one more added, in the group `Errors`, written once as ` errors`.
then: Expects one `lone-child` warning: 'Standard EX-STD-CODE's group "Imports" has only one standard rule, EX-STD-CODE-R01; merge it into a neighboring group, or give it more.', and none for the Errors group, whose two members match in any case.

title: A product kind's group with one member is a lone-child warning
when: Declares a product kind with a group_name field and puts three of its records under one domain, two in one group and one alone in another.
then: Expects one lone-child warning, naming the group of one and its member.

title: An aggregate with more entities than the limit is a warning naming it, the count and the limit
when: With `max_entities_per_aggregate` 3.
then: Expects no warning for an aggregate with 3 entities, and an `aggregate-too-large` warning for one with 4, naming it, the count and the limit and saying to split it.

title: Without the setting the entities limit is 7
when: With no `product_setting` row.
then: Expects no warning for an aggregate with 7 entities, and a warning for one with 8.

title: Every problem of a product shows in one place, as the data is after its latest change
when: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, the Owner opens the product's Checks page and a data file gains an unused view while it is open.
then: The page counts the product's errors and warnings, and counts the new errors (the unused view, and the gap it opens in a strict product) without a reload.

title: A product's problems read lists its own by check, errors first, then the workspace's, counted, and leaves out every other product's
when: Reads list-problems over two products with a run of the checks whose problems are about each product's records, about no record and about an ID no record has; then without a run; then through the CLI, the MCP tool and HTTP over a run of the checks.
then: Expects each product's own problems by check, errors first, the workspace's for both, the counts, a refusal without a run, and the same answer from the CLI and HTTP.

title: A pattern rule test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern is an error
when: Loads a pattern rule test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern, then has the domain follow it.
then: Expects a pattern-rule-test-outside-followers error naming the domain and pattern, and none once the domain follows it.

title: A manual test whose file names neither its ID, nor an ID it proves, nor its key is reported
when: Points the complete product's manual integration test at `manual/mail.md`, once with that file present but never naming the test, and once with no such file.
then: Expects a `manual-test-file-silent` warning on `EX-INT01-T01` when the file exists and never names it, and none when the file is missing.

title: A product's essential records are listed alone, by domain, with their kind, title and lead text
when: Lists the complete product's essential records, as the query and its text, then asks for a product there is not.
then: Expects the Lending domain's essential records in ID order and those in no domain last, with no technical record, pattern, slot or test, the count and text to match, and the unknown product refused.

title: The check-and-fix skill has the Agent hold each essential record to the domain-expert test before proposing a change
when: Reads the plugin's check-and-fix skill.
then: Expects it to run the essential review's list, ask the domain-expert question of each record, list what fails with why for the Owner, and change no essential record on that alone.

title: A strict check fails on any warning, saying it is strict and why; a check that is not strict passes
when: Runs lathe check, lathe check with its machine-readable option, and the check tool, on the complete product with three warnings from its titles, no gap and no error, not strict and then strict.
then: Expects status 0 and no word of strictness when it is not strict, and status 1 with a strict-check error, a count line saying the product is strict and why it fails, the strictness in the machine-readable result, and the check tool's answer a failure saying the same, when it is.

title: A strict check passes at its accepted count, and fails below it, saying to lower the count
when: Runs lathe check on the complete product with three warnings from its titles and no gap, strict and accepting three, then accepting five.
then: Expects status 0 with a count line naming the accepted count as a recorded deviation, then status 1 with a strict-check error saying to lower the count to three.

title: Making the check strict accepts no more warnings than the product has now, and keeps its limits
when: With TL's limits set, makes its check strict accepting two warnings over a checks' run holding two, then tries three, a count for a check that is not strict, and no run at all.
then: Expects the row to hold the strictness and keep the limits, each later try refused with nothing changed, accepting none to be plain strict, and not strict to drop both.

title: A strict check fails on any gap, whatever warnings it accepts, saying how many and how to list them; a check that is not strict passes
when: Runs lathe check and the check tool on the complete product with a technical file not written, so two records are not built, and its three warnings, not strict and then strict accepting three warnings.
then: Expects status 0 and no word of strictness when it is not strict, and status 1 with a strict-gaps error naming two gaps and how to list them, no strict-check error, a count line saying warnings and gaps fail and the check fails on two gaps, and the check tool's answer a failure saying the same, when it is.

title: A strict product's check fails with one strict-gaps error at one gap or more and passes at none; a product that is not strict never fails on gaps
when: Judges three products' strictness over a checks' run and coverage: TL strict accepting one warning with one warning and one gap, LA strict with none, EX not strict with three gaps, then TL again with no gap.
then: Expects one strict-gaps error, for TL, naming its one gap, how to list them and that no count of gaps is accepted, none at zero gaps, and each product's gaps, failures and count line to say the same, with nothing for EX.

title: The product's own technology words replace the last
when: Runs set the product's technology words through the command on a temporary product that holds the records it works on.
then: Expects what the requirement states: the product's own technology words replace the last.

title: Words that break the settings' rules are refused
when: Runs set the product's technology words through the command on a temporary product that holds the records it works on. Then runs it so that it breaks a rule.
then: Expects what the requirement states: words that break the settings' rules are refused.

title: A changed check runs as changed on the next check
when: On a temporary product, adds a house check, changes its severity with `lathe check change-check`, and checks again.
then: Expects the problem the check reports at the new severity.

title: A change to one of Lathe's own checks is refused
when: Tries to change one of Lathe's own checks with `lathe check change-check`.
then: Expects it refused as read-only, and the check unchanged.

title: A removed check no longer reports
when: On a temporary product, adds a house check, removes it with `lathe check remove-check`, and checks again.
then: Expects the problems it reported gone.

title: A removal of one of Lathe's own checks is refused
when: Tries to remove one of Lathe's own checks with `lathe check remove-check`.
then: Expects it refused as read-only, and the check still running.

title: The Reader finds a record in a domain
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a domain's page, finds a record in it by its ID and then by its title, and opens it.
then: The domain's page lists its records by stage and kind; quick find (Cmd/Ctrl+K) finds the record by its ID and by words of its title, and choosing it opens the record's page.

title: The Reader reads a product in its stage folders
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a product and unfolds Shared and each domain's five stages in the nav.
then: Shared lists what the product shares, and each domain unfolds into its five stages, Domain model, Use cases, Interface design, Technical specification and Test plan, each holding one folder per kind with its records.

title: The folder tree read gives Shared and each domain its stages, a folder per kind and what folds under each record
when: Reads get-folder-tree for one of two products, with terms one of which builds on another.
then: Expects Shared and the product's domain only, an aggregate's entity and invariant folded under it, terms bottom-up, a stage's one folder shown directly, and the product's pattern with its rule under Shared.

title: The Reader reads the technical specification and test plan by kind
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a domain's Technical specification and Test plan in the nav, on the domain page and in the graph.
then: The domain's technical records and tests appear grouped by kind, the same kinds in the same order, in the nav's Technical specification and Test plan, on the domain page and as the graph's groups.

title: The Reader follows a record's links
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: From a record's page, follows a link out and a link in to the records at their ends, then goes back.
then: Each link under Links out and Links in opens the record at its other end, and Back returns to the first record's page where it was left.

title: The record summaries read places each record of a product's space and gives its file, line, digest and the links among them
when: Reads list-record-summaries for one of two products, with a value object one domain uses and then two, a link, and a part row changed.
then: Expects each record placed up its parents, by its ID or in the one domain that uses it, nothing of the other product, no column beyond its summary, the links among them, and a digest that changes only when its rows do.

title: The space's record index holds each record's summary with its children and its links both ways
when: Builds a space's record index from the summaries and meta model reads over the served data.
then: Expects each record with its parent, product and domain, its data file and line and no other column, and each link both ways.

title: The Reader walks the model as a graph
when: In each layout of the graph, clicks a labeled box in view.
then: Expects the address to change to the clicked box's page, that box drawn as the focus, the header strip's breadcrumb shown and, for a record, `.header-strip-id` showing its ID.

title: The Reader walks the graph through the nav's groups
when: Opens Lathe's graph and clicks the boxes of `LA-EXP`, its Use cases stage, an aggregate heading and a use case in turn.
then: Expects each click to move the address to the box's page and draw it as the focus, with nothing outside the graph's boxes moving.

title: The Reader reads a record as wiki, graph or model
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a record at its address and reads it in the wiki card, then switches the stage behind it to the Graph, the ERD and the Trace, with the mouse and from the keyboard.
then: The record opens at `/<id>` with its page in the wiki card; the Graph, ERD and Trace buttons of the stage switch, and Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2 and Ctrl+3, change only the stage behind the card, the address keeping `?stage=`, and the card shows the same record throughout.

title: The Reader reads a flow step by step
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a flow's page and reads each path's steps in order, with what each invokes, where it happens and what it fulfills.
then: Each path lists its steps in order, and each step shows the command or query it invokes, the view it happens in and the requirements it fulfills, each a link to its record.

title: The Reader reads a domain's endpoints and integrations
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a command or a query to find its endpoint, and an integration to find the steps that exchange with it.
then: The command's or query's page links to the endpoint that exposes it, and the integration's page lists the flow steps that exchange with it, each a link to its record.

title: The Reader moves between products as spaces
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a page in one product, switches to another product's space from the rail, then back.
then: The other product's space shows only its own records, problems and counts; switching back opens the first product on the page last visited in it.

title: The rail shows with two products and not with one
when: Opens Lathe's workspace of two products in Chromium, then the same with its own product alone.
then: Expects the rail with both spaces; with one product no rail, the product's name and icon at the top of the nav.

title: The Reader explores several places at once in tabs
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens several records in tabs, changes each one's stage and scroll, and reloads the page.
then: After the reload the same tabs are open with the same one active, and each comes back on its own page, stage and scroll.

title: A record ID in Claude's reply focuses the stage, and Cmd or Ctrl+click opens it in a new tab
when: Draws a reply naming a record and clicks its ID plainly and with Cmd.
then: Expects the new place opened on Cmd+click, the stage left, and the stage focused on a plain click.

title: A nav section stays as the Reader left it
when: Folds the Tools section with Fold or unfold a nav section.
then: Reads the nav rows back from the browser storage, then unfolds the section.

title: Cycling activates the next or previous tab
when: With three tabs open, cycles forward and back through the command.
then: Expects the active tab to wrap from the last to the first, step back, and to stay with one tab.

title: A duplicated tab is a copy of the whole place
when: Keeps a camera for a tab, then duplicates the tab with Duplicate a tab.
then: Expects a copy right after the tab, active, with the same place and the same camera.

title: The wiki card's width stays within its limits
when: Resizes the wiki card past each limit, then resets it.
then: Expects the width held at the limit, then none (the default).

title: The chat's width stays within its limits
when: Resizes the chat past each limit, then resets it.
then: Expects the width held at the limit, then none (the default).

title: Highlight changes follows the Reader for the session
when: Turns Highlight changes on, then off.
then: Expects the session settings to say on, in the session storage, then off.

title: The baseline is one of the three the Reader can choose
when: Chooses each of the three baselines, then another.
then: Expects each of the three kept and the other refused, leaving the last choice.

title: A tab's entry keeps where the page was
when: Notes a scroll in a tab's entry, then steps the tab back to it.
then: Expects the entry to hold the scroll noted.

title: After a turn that writes, its records can be put under review: lit on the stage and walked through with their diffs
when: With a turn that changes a command, starts the review and ends it.
then: Expects the review bar with the turn named, the position and diff shown, Highlight changes on, and the bar gone on Done.

title: The Reader reads a domain's ERD
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person reads the pages as the Reader does.
when: Opens a domain on the ERD stage, then one of its aggregates.
then: The ERD draws the domain's aggregates with their entities, fields and the links between them; opening an aggregate draws that aggregate's own entities and fields.

title: The ERD read gives a product's domains, aggregates with their entities (root first) and fields, and its lines, nothing of another product
when: Reads get-erd for one of two products, with a has-one link and a field typed by another aggregate.
then: Expects each box with its parent, root and empty marks, each entity's fields with their types, a has-one line and a reference line to the other aggregate's root, and a refusal for a product that is not there.

title: The Reader reads a record's history in the wiki card
when: Makes the suite's data a git repository with twenty-two commits that touch a domain and one change not committed, opens the domain's graph, shows its history in the wiki card, opens a commit and loads more.
then: Expects the history to show the change not committed and `Retitle 21`, opening `Retitle 20` to show `Exploring 20`, and Load more to reach the first commit, `The data`.

title: The record diff finds records added, removed and changed field by field, with their part rows and links
when: In one store write, retitles a use case and gives it a goal, an actor and a link, removes another use case and adds a third; then diffs the rows before and after.
then: Expects the three records changed, removed and added in ID order; the changed one's title and goal before and after, its actor added and its link added; the added and removed ones with no rows listed; nothing for the same rows; the reverse diff undoing it; and a base plus its delta giving the rows back.

title: The record changes read lists each record added, removed and changed since the baseline, per product
when: Reads list-record-changes for a product with a baseline, and with none.
then: Expects each record that differs with its change and nothing of another product, and with no baseline the reason and no change.

title: The Record changes read over HTTP compares with the baseline its since names, read from git
when: Reads GET /api/record-changes/list-record-changes for a product in a temporary git repo since the last commit, since the branch left main and since a noted commit, then in a folder with no git, at a commit that does not exist, with a since that is no baseline, with no product and for an unknown product.
then: Expects the records changed since each baseline with their fields before and after; no baseline and no change, with the reason, with no git or no such commit, and when git cannot give a data file, whose failed read is not kept; 400 for a bad since or no product; 422 for an unknown product.

title: Every stage marks the records a reload added, changed and removed, with dots only under reduced motion
when: Opens an aggregate's graph at depth 3 and reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, then with the added one gone, then with the renamed one gone.
then: Expects the renamed command marked changed and the new one added, the command added and then removed gone with no ghost, and a ghost where the removed command was.

title: Highlight changes dims the unchanged records against each baseline, and since I last looked moves when it is turned off or the product left
when: Reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, turns Highlight changes on, picks since the branch left main, then since I last looked, and turns it off.
then: Expects a count of 2, the changed command at full strength and every unchanged box dimmed to a fifth, the new command's box carrying the New pill and the renamed one's the Changed pill, the branch baseline asked for and kept in the session setting, the last look kept at the last commit with the same 2 changes, and turning it off moving the last look to now with a count of 0 and both commands in its delta.

title: A record removed that the baseline had leaves only its ghost, and one new since the baseline then removed leaves nothing
when: Opens the page with a command already added since the baseline, turns Highlight changes on, removes it, then removes a command the baseline had.
then: Expects the added one gone with no box and no ghost, and the baseline one gone with its ghost and no box.

title: A changed record's wiki card shows its changes, and an added one says New since its baseline
when: Opens a command's page, reloads the data with the command renamed and a new one added, then goes to the new command.
then: Expects the wiki card's Changes section to say Changed since the last commit with the old title struck out and the new one inserted, and the new command's card to say New since the last commit.

title: The wiki card lists the links a changed record gained and lost, beside each field old → new
when: Opens a command's page, reloads the data with the command retitled and redescribed, one event it raises replaced by another.
then: Expects the Changes section to list the title and the description each old → new, and the links "Added raises" the new event and "Removed raises" the old one.

title: The Changes panel lists the changes newest first by record, a click focuses one, and its toggle counts them
when: Reloads the data twice, renaming a command and then an aggregate, opens the Changes panel from its toggle and clicks the command's card.
then: Expects the toggle to count 2, the aggregate's card before the command's, and the click to focus the command with the panel still open.

title: Roll-ups count the new, changed and removed records under each container, and the nav shows them beside each folder
when: Counts the changes under each place of a small tree with a record added, one changed and one removed, writes the roll-up text, and counts the same changes for the nav's folders and domains.
then: Expects each container to count only the changes strictly under it, the text "1 new · 2 changed · 1 removed" leaving out zeros, a removed record counted under the nearest container its ID names, and the nav's counts by folder and domain the same.

title: With Highlight changes on, the Graph's boxes carry their pill and each container its roll-up, and the nav shows the counts
when: Reloads the data with a command renamed and one added, turns Highlight changes on at depth 3, and reads the Graph's scene and the nav.
then: Expects the new command's box to carry the New pill and the renamed one the Changed pill, their entity's box the roll-up "1 new · 1 changed", and the nav to show the counts beside the domain.

then: Expects only the boxes whose centers lie outside counted, on the side they lie, and none for an edge with nothing past it.

title: Next change and Previous change step through the changed records in ID order, around at the ends
when: Steps forward and back through a walk of changed records from a changed focus, from an unchanged one, past each end, and through an empty walk.
then: Expects the next record after the focus (or the first), the previous one before it (or the last), numbers compared by value, and nothing for an empty walk.

then: Expects the focus to follow to the renamed command with Follow still on, then Follow off with the note that you moved the camera, and off again with the note that you moved the focus.

title: Each tab keeps its own view
when: Sets depth 2 and hides a kind in the graph, then reloads.
then: Expects the depth and the hidden kind kept.

title: Back and Forward stay in the active tab

title: A product kind's record that proves an obligation has its file checked as a test's

title: A file a test names is read for test cases, whatever its name

title: Each domain counts its own tests by state, which every test gives

then: Expects 11 automated, 2 manual and 0 not automated yet in `EX-LEND`, and 1 automated, the standard rule's test, outside every domain.

title: The tests by state read counts each scope's tests as automated, manual and not automated yet, the product's own scope first

then: Expects the product's own scope then each domain's counts, its text one line per scope, and a refusal for no such product.

title: A test data set sits under a domain, and any kind of test starts from any number of them
when: Adds a second data set, links two kinds of test to data sets, links a use case to one, and names a data set for another domain.
then: Every test kind and only a test starts from a data set; the use case's link is refused, and so is the misnamed ID.

title: Each Test data set command changes one test data set through its repository, and one a test starts from stays
when: Adds, changes, reads and removes a test data set with its own commands, then removes one a test starts from, and runs its commands from the CLI and the MCP tools.
then: Expects each command to write only the test_data_set table, its domain never to change, and the removal of the used one refused naming the test that starts from it.

title: A data set no test starts from is an error; a missing file is an error when an automated test starts from it, else a warning
when: Unlinks every test from the complete product's data set, removes its seed file, makes its one test not automated yet, and names a folder of fixtures.
then: test-data-set-unused is an error; test-data-set-file-missing is an error, then a warning; a folder gives no problem.

title: A domain's test data sets are listed, and one is read with the tests that start from it
when: Lists the lending domain's test data sets, then reads one whole.
then: Expects it listed, and read with the integration test that starts from it.

title: Change a test data set given nothing is refused and the data files stay as they were
when: Runs the command with no fields on a product that holds a record of every kind.
then: The command is refused with a reason, and no data file changes.

title: Remove a test data set given nothing is refused and the data files stay as they were
when: Runs the command with no fields on a product that holds a record of every kind.
then: The command is refused with a reason, and no data file changes.

title: A test data set moved to another domain takes its ID there, and its tests follow
when: Moves the lending domain's test data set to the catalog domain.
then: Expects it under the catalog domain's ID, and the test that starts from it naming that ID.

title: A test whose file lacks its ID is reported as an error
when: Loads the complete product with the invariant test's file not naming `EX-LEND-INV01-T`.
then: Expects the only gap to be `proved EX-LEND-INV01`, and no gaps when the file names the test.

title: A state outside the three, or none, is refused
when: Loads a test with the state someday, one with Manual, and one with no state.
then: Expects the first two refused as values outside automated, manual and not automated yet, and the third as a missing required column.

title: Only an automated test needs a file, and only a manual test gives a reason
when: Loads an automated test with no file, a manual test with no reason, a reason on an automated test, and a test not automated yet naming a file that does not exist.
then: Expects the first three refused, and the last to load with one test-file-missing warning and no error.

title: A level outside the five, or none, is refused
when: Loads a test with the level smoke, and one with no level.
then: Expects the first refused as a value outside the five levels, and the second as a missing required column.

title: A pattern rule is an obligation under a pattern, for proof alone
when: Loads the complete product with no pattern rule test.
then: Expects pattern_rule an obligation, its rule designed and built though nothing designs it, and only its proof missing.

title: A domain that does not follow the pattern does not owe its rules
when: Adds a second domain, `EX-SHOP`, whose use cases do not follow the complete product's pattern.
then: Expects a pattern rule total of 0 in `EX-SHOP`.

title: A domain's own pattern rule test proves the rule there alone
when: A second domain follows the pattern with no test of its own, then with one not automated yet.
then: Expects the rule proved in the first domain only, and not automated yet in the second once its test is.

title: Not-proved warnings name the pattern rule and the domain
when: Two domains owe a rule and neither proves it, then one has a test not automated yet.
then: Expects one not-proved warning per domain naming the rule and the domain, the second time saying the test there is not automated yet.

title: A pattern that no use case follows is a warning
when: Loads the complete product with its setting values, `follows` links and pattern rule tests removed, so no use case or domain follows its pattern.
then: Expects one `pattern-not-followed` warning on `EX-PAT-ACT`: "No use case or domain follows pattern EX-PAT-ACT, so its 1 rule is not counted in any domain's coverage."

title: An obligation outside every domain counts in Shared
when: Declares an obligation kind under the product, with one record.
then: Expects it counted and not proved in the product's Shared coverage, and no pattern rule there.

title: A pattern sits under the product with its settings, and use cases or domains follow it
when: A domain follows the pattern; a requirement tries to.
then: The domain loads with no pattern problem; the requirement is refused.

title: Each Pattern command changes one pattern through its repository, its settings given in order
when: Builds a pattern with its settings, a rule and a rule test with its own commands, replaces its settings, removes a rule, then removes a followed pattern and drops a setting a rule depends on, and runs its commands from the CLI and the MCP tools.
then: Expects the settings saved in the order given, a rule removed with its tests, and the removal of the followed pattern and of the depended-on setting refused, nothing changed.

title: A product's patterns are listed, and one is read with its settings, rules and slots
when: Lists the product's patterns, then reads one whole.
then: Expects it listed, and read with its setting, its rule and its slot.

title: A use case has one flow, the same through every interface, whose steps need a path and a position, fulfill its requirements, invoke a command or query, exchange with integrations and may be a variant
when: Reads the schema and loads the complete product.
then: Expects an interface under its product with a required kind of web app, API, CLI, agent tools, desktop or other; a flow under its use case, one per use case; and each step's path and position required, with what it fulfills, invokes, exchanges with and the interface it is a variant of.

title: A well-formed flow raises no step problem; a second flow for the use case, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke are refused
when: With a well-formed flow, writes a second flow for its use case, a repeated position, a step fulfilling another use case and a second invoke.
then: No step-order problem on the good flow; each broken row is refused.

title: Each use case command changes one use case through its repository and is refused, changing nothing, when it breaks a rule
when: Runs each kind of Use case command on a store: adds, changes, moves, links a step, and gives inputs that break a rule, an unknown field, a missing one or a write to another table.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the Use case aggregate's tables, and each refused one to name its rule and reason and leave every data file as it was.

title: Only repositories write data files, a handler loads only its own aggregate, and every command has its definition
when: Reads every source file's imports, every command definition and Lathe's command records.
then: Expects only repositories to import data-files.ts, only command handlers to import repositories and each only its own aggregate's, and every command of an aggregate with a slice to have its definition.

title: A flow step moves to a position of its path or another, and every path stays numbered 1, 2, 3
when: Moves the last step of a flow first, then onto a new path, then to a position past the end of its path.
then: Expects each path numbered 1, 2, 3 after each move, and the last move refused, changing nothing.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group, a column whose renaming changes no ID
when: A group is set on each of the five kinds, then renamed.
then: group_name is optional on all five; no ID changes and the renamed group loads.

title: A domain's use cases are listed by group, and one is read with its requirements, flow and tests
when: Lists the lending domain's use cases, then reads one whole.
then: Expects it listed, and read with its requirement and test and its flow's step.

title: A use case with no domain, or an ID that names another domain than its own, is refused
when: Loads a use case with no domain, then one in a domain whose ID its own does not start with.
then: Expects a refusal that the domain is required, and one that its ID starts with its domain's.

title: A pattern rule is owed by each domain that follows its pattern, itself or through a use case, and proved there by one pattern rule test
when: Loads one domain that follows a pattern through a use case and has its rule test, and another that follows it itself with none.
then: The rule is owed in both and proved only in the first; a second test for one rule and domain is refused; a test naming a non-follower is an error.

title: Change a pattern rule given nothing is refused and the data files stay as they were
when: Runs the command with no fields on a product that holds a record of every kind.
then: The command is refused with a reason, and no data file changes.

title: A flow's ID is its use case's ID and FL
when: A flow through a second interface is added with the right ID, a wrong one, and through another product's interface.
then: The first is accepted; flow-id-interface refuses the second and reference-crosses-product the third.

title: Every aggregate's next-id query answers the shape its kind's id_pattern gives
when: Asks each next-id query for the next ID under the parent of every numbered record in Lathe's own spec.
then: Each answer has the record's prefix and at least its digits, and is past the record's number (a flow's is its use case's and FL).

title: An interface that offers no use case is a gap
when: Adds a second interface that no flow goes through.
then: An interface-without-flow gap names it.

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
when: Loads a use case with no flow.
then: Expects a use-case-without-flow gap in its domain, and no error.

title: A UC requirement no step of its flow fulfills is reported as not designed
when: The only fulfills link to a requirement is removed.
then: A designed gap and a not-designed warning, for that requirement only.

title: A step an offering interface cannot reach is reported, for each kind of interface
when: Makes the complete product's interface an API, with its steps in no view.
then: step-unreached warns of each step whose command or query an offering web app or desktop has no view for, an API no endpoint for, and a CLI or agent tools no record of its own for; a variant of another interface and an interface of kind other are left be.

title: A variant of an interface that does not offer its use case is an error
when: Makes a step a variant of an interface that does not offer its use case.
then: variant-not-offered reports the step as an error, naming the interface and the use case.

title: A use case with a flow no interface offers is warned of
when: Removes every interface's offer of a use case that has a flow.
then: flow-not-offered warns of the use case.

title: An interface that offers a use case none of whose actors is among its roles is warned of
when: Gives an interface roles that are none of an offered use case's actors.
then: interface-actor-not-the-use-case warns of the interface, naming its roles.

title: A command line or agent tools reaches a step through a record of the product's own that presents its command or query, scoped as a view is
when: Gives the complete product a command line that offers a use case and an interface design kind of its own that presents commands and queries, then has one record present the step's command and query, under no interface, under that interface, and under another.
then: step-unreached leaves the steps be while the record presents them and sits under no interface or under that interface, and warns of them when it sits under another interface or presents nothing; the use case read model names the record as where each step is carried out.

title: A path whose positions skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap
when: Loads two steps of one flow on one path, written `refused` and `Refused`, at positions 2 and 3 with no step at 1.
then: Expects one `step-order` error, on the step at position 2.

title: The same step written per interface is an error
when: Makes a step of the complete product the web app's variant and adds the CLI's variant invoking the same command, then makes one every interface's, puts both on one interface, or has them invoke different operations.
then: step-repeated-per-interface reports each of the two variants as an error naming the other, and leaves the other three be.

title: A use case: Change a use case is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs change-use-case naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.
then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: A UC requirement: Add a UC requirement is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs add-uc-requirement naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.
then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: A UC requirement: Change a UC requirement is refused with every reason, or applied

title: A use case test: Remove a use case test is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs remove-use-case-test naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.
then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record removed.

title: A flow test: Change a flow test is refused with every reason, or applied

then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: Each offering interface's version of a flow is derived: where each step is carried out, its actor, the variants left out
when: Reads a use case whose flow a web app and an API offer, with a variant only the web app does.
then: Expects the web app's version to carry the step out in the view that presents its command and to keep its variant, the API's in the endpoint that exposes it without the variant, and each with the first of the use case's actors it lists.

title: A flow test: Remove a flow test is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs remove-flow-test naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.
then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record removed.

then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: A pattern: Remove a pattern is refused with every reason, or applied

then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record removed.

then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: A slot: Change a slot is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs change-slot naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.
then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: A slot: Remove a slot is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs remove-slot naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.

title: A flow step: Move a flow step is refused with every reason, or applied
when: Runs move-flow-step naming a record that is not there, then with the right input.
then: Expects the refusal with its reason and no change, then the record written as given.

title: A use case goes whole, and a record referenced from outside what goes stays
when: Removes a use case with a requirement, flow and step, then a use case another aggregate follows and asks about, a requirement a step fulfills, a flow with its steps and a test a business outcome is measured by.
then: Expects the first use case and its flow to go with everything under them, and every other removal to be refused, naming each referrer.

title: A use case, and everything under it, belongs to its result's domain and counts in its coverage
when: A use case is moved to another domain, with a result there.
then: Everything under a use case carries its domain and the pattern none; after the move the use case and everything under it are in the new domain and count in its coverage.

title: Each record moved to another domain takes its IDs, with everything under it, and nothing names an old ID
when: Moves a domain's records, a use case with a result there, and a record to a domain of another product.
then: Expects each moved record and everything under it to take the new domain's ID, no record to name an old ID, and the domain of another product to be refused.

title: A use case moved to a domain where its ID is taken takes the next free number there, with everything in it
when: Moves a use case, with a requirement, to a domain whose use cases already have its number.
then: Expects it to take one past the highest use case number in that domain, its requirement and actors to follow its new ID, and the other domain's use case to be untouched.

title: A requirement moved to another use case takes its next number, its tests follow, and one a step fulfills stays
when: Moves a requirement no step fulfills to a use case of another domain, then a requirement a step fulfills.
then: Expects the first to take the other use case's next requirement number with its tests renamed and every mention following, and the second refused, naming the step.

title: A test is small unless it says volume or worst case, and marks itself smoke or external only by saying yes
when: Gives a test volume with both markers, worst case, small, and each marker as no.
then: Every test kind has the three optional columns; volume, worst case and the markers as yes load; small is refused as not one of the sizes, and a marker of no by its check.

title: A test changed to automated with no file is refused
when: Tries to change a test not automated yet to automated with no file.
then: Expects it refused, naming the file, and the test unchanged.

title: Removing a use case a step carries out is refused naming the step, and removing the journey keeps it
when: Removes a use case a journey step carries out, then the journey, then the use case.
then: Expects the first refused naming the step, the journey gone with its steps and test, and the use case then removed.
